passage.text: The relationship between Gestalt therapy and psychopathology has not been easy, for epistemological, historical, and political reasons. Nevertheless, Gestalt therapy has a specific psychopathological understanding, as every psychotherapeutic model does, whether explicitly or implicitly. The humanistic insight that each person and each experience is unique always remains valuable. The goal of developing a Gestalt psychopathology is not to label clients, but to understand their suffering from an experiential and relational theoretical perspective. Such an understanding gives therapists specific support and clear guidelines for experiential and relational work.

source.title: Article Aesthetic Diagnosis in Gestalt Therapy
